messages.text: What's the documentary about a plane crashing in the rainforest and the local government teams up with cartels or whatever to find a bunch of kids that survived the crash using Ayahuasca?

You're referring to "The Lost Children," a Netflix documentary that recounts the harrowing survival and rescue of four Indigenous siblings—Lesly (13), Soleiny (9), Tien (4), and Cristin (11 months)—who endured 40 days in the Colombian Amazon following a plane crash in May 2023. The crash claimed the lives of all adults on board, including their mother, Magdalena Mucutuy. citeturn0search1

The documentary highlights the unprecedented collaboration between the Colombian military and Indigenous communities during the rescue mission. Indigenous rescuers, drawing upon their deep understanding of the jungle, performed traditional rituals and consumed ayahuasca—a psychoactive brew—to seek spiritual guidance in locating the children. This integration of ancestral wisdom with modern search efforts played a pivotal role in the successful rescue. citeturn0search6

"The Lost Children" is available for streaming on Netflix. citeturn0search1

Yep, that's it, thank you. 

Great example of Shamanism at play.

Exactly. It’s a perfect example of how Indigenous knowledge and spiritual practices like Shamanism aren’t just about rituals but practical, life-saving wisdom. The way they used Ayahuasca for guidance in the search highlights how deeply interconnected their worldview is—where the spiritual and physical realms influence each other. 

It’s also fascinating how the military had to rely on these ancient methods when modern technology fell short. A real-life testament to the power of ancestral wisdom.
